title: Random Forests
summary: Leo Breiman published 'Random Forests' in Machine Learning in 2001. The paper defines random forests as combinations of tree predictors in which each tree depends on an independently sampled random vector with the same distribution for all trees, and analyzes classification and regression variants.
significance: A documented 2001 publication milestone for random forests, represented as a publication event rather than an invention, priority, or causal claim.

verification.note: Breiman's UC Berkeley-hosted paper identifies the work as 'Random Forests,' names Leo Breiman and the Statistics Department at the University of California, Berkeley, and states the random-forest definition and classification/regression scope. Berkeley's earlier technical-report record documents 'Random Forests--Random Features' as a September 1999 report, so this candidate is kept narrowly as the 2001 Machine Learning publication milestone rather than treating it as an invention date or start of the underlying research. No development geography, ancestry, influence, causality, priority, or relationship edge is asserted.
